newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Greece expels 3,500 Albanians in crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Greece expels 3,500 Albanians in crackdown.

text.p: Greece has expelled at least 3,500 Albanian immigrants since Friday, many of whom complain they fell prey to armed robbers as soon as they crossed into their homeland.
Border police said on Wednesday some 700 Albanians caught without the correct papers had been sent back from Greece in the past 24 hours alone.

Police captain Arben Haka at the Kakavije border point said many had recently gone to look for work in Greece and had been caught around the Greek city of Ioannina near the border. Others were being brought back by bus from further afield.
Alfred Pali, 22, from the village of Borizane in Kruje district, and Agustin Speli, 21, from Fushe Kruje, said they had crossed the border 10 times in the last nine months.
Three times they had managed to work for about a month, while the other seven times Greek police caught them and brought them back.
They said three armed men had stopped a group of 40 expelled Albanians soon after they crossed the border and taken their clothes and belongings, leaving them with just some bread and tomatoes.
"Now we are praying to God to go back to our families. We have eaten nothing and have no money in our pockets. We shall plead wth drivers to take us back home," Speli said.
Buses and taxis do not operate in the border area because of the security risks.
On Tuesday, Kakavije police freed a young man kidnapped with his Mercedes car seven or eight hours earlier by a gang from the nearby Delvine district.

Romanian troops of the Multinational Protection Force withdrew from Gjirokaster last week. Their mandate was to ensure security for elections and aid deliveries, not to take on the gunmen, but local people found their presence reassuring.
Residents say life in the town is relatively normal during the mornings but quietens down after midday. Shopkeepers open until midday then take their stock home for safekeeping.
